content: She was involved in the preparation of GRADE tables for a remuneration of US $6,400. Additionally, she contributed to the preparation of GRADE tables for another project, receiving US $3,200 for her role. At McGill University, she served as a systematic review author for a project evaluating Xpert MTB/RIF and Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra for the diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance in adults, for which she was compensated US $16,970. At the University of Washington, Department of Medicine in Seattle, she worked as a systematic review author on a project focused on symptom screening for active tuberculosis in pregnant women living with HIV, receiving US $1,000 for her contribution. She also collaborated with FIND (Foundation for Innovative New Diagnostics) as a systematic review author for a project assessing commercial products for preserving clinical specimens, for which she was paid US $3,200. For the World Health Organization (WHO), she acted as a systematic review author for a project evaluating the GenoType® MTBDRsl assay, earning US $12,000. Additionally, she participated as a member of the Guideline Development Group for the LAMP assay and contributed to a webinar held on January 27, 2016, for which she did not receive any remuneration. She co-authored a three-year grant funded by the Canadian Institutes of Health Research (CIHR) through McGill University, Montreal. The grant, titled “Evaluating diagnostic accuracy of tests and decision rules in the absence of a perfect reference standard,” spanned from 2018 to 2020. In 2018, she received financial support from McGill University to attend two conferences: the Methods for Evaluating Medical Tests & Biomarkers conference held on July 2–3, 2018, in Utrecht, and the Union World Conference on Lung Health held on October 24–27, 2018, in The Hague. She also received support to attend the Union World Conference on Lung Health in 2019 and 2020. In 2020, she was provided with financial support amounting to US $2,400 to purchase a laptop and software. Apart from these instances, she did not receive any additional remuneration. The project was completed in October 2020.
